persona.bio: Rosa, 38, runs her own wedding planning business with about twenty weddings a year. Everything runs through Gmail: couples, venues, florists, photographers, caterers. She answers inquiry emails, writes the same welcome and contract emails again and again, chases vendors and couples who haven't replied, and keeps budgets, timelines and guest lists in Google Sheets. She uses ChatGPT every day and pays for it. She has saved instructions about herself in it but never connected it to Gmail.

path.role: You run your own wedding planning business, handling inquiries, vendor bookings, timelines and client messages.

steps.title: Answering messages, drafted in your inbox
steps.read: Your replies now start inside Gmail. Help me write drafts each one from a short line you type, and you read it before you send it. That keeps your answers warm and quick when new messages come in many times a day, without starting from an old email each time.

material.label: Your starting lines
items: Thank them for reaching out about their [month] wedding and suggest a call on [day and time] to talk about their date and budget.
Thank them for their interest, say I have openings for [month], and ask for their date, guest count and rough budget.
Say I am booked on [date], thank them kindly, and offer to point them to [another planner or resource] if they would like.
Confirm our call on [day and time], say I will send a short list of questions beforehand, and tell them I am looking forward to it.
Reply to a vendor who sent a quote: thank them, say I am reviewing it with my client, and I will answer by [day].
Answer a client’s question about [topic] in a calm, reassuring way and say I will confirm the details by [day].
Tell a client their timeline draft is attached, ask them to read it, and send changes by [day].

material.label: Tone notes for the buttons
items: Friendly: use this for new inquiries and past clients. The draft should sound warm and welcoming, like how I talk on a call.
Formalize: use this for vendor contracts, venues and anything about money or dates. It should sound clear and professional.
Shorten: use this for quick confirmations, like a time or a delivery. One or two sentences is enough.
If a draft sounds too stiff or too salesy, press Friendly, then read it again and fix any detail that is wrong.
If a draft adds anything I did not say, such as a price, a date or a promise, I delete it before sending.

steps.title: Your vendor follow ups, drafted from your inbox for your OK
steps.read: When a vendor goes quiet, ChatGPT looks through your Gmail and drafts the follow up for you. It waits for your OK on each one, so nothing goes out until you have read it. Chasing stops being something you write by hand and remember on your own.

material.label: Instructions for your assistant
items: I run my own wedding planning business. Look in my Gmail for emails I sent to vendors, like venues, caterers, florists and photographers, where I asked a question or needed a booking, quote or confirmation and have had no reply. Count an email as waiting if I sent the last message and [number] business days have passed. For each one, write a short follow up to that same person, about that same email, in my voice: warm, plain and polite, never pushy. Mention the event date only if it is in the thread. Do not invent prices, dates or promises. Give me a list showing who each draft is for, the subject of the email, and the draft itself. Do not send anything. I will read each draft and decide.

material.label: Your follow up wording
items: Hi [first name], I wanted to check in on my email from [day] about [topic]. Have you had a chance to look? I would love to confirm things for [client event date] if you can let me know by [day]. Thank you!

Hi [first name], following up again on [topic]. I know things get busy. Could you let me know by [day] whether you can hold [date] for my client? If I do not hear back, I may need to look at other options. Thanks so much!

safeUse: Never type a client’s full name, phone number, home address or email into ChatGPT. Use square brackets or a first name only.
Keep contract terms, payment details and card or bank numbers out of any chat. Add them yourself after.
Leave out guest lists, allergy or health details and anything a couple told you in private.
Read every draft before it goes out and check dates, times, prices and names against your Sheet.
Keep Always ask on, so nothing is sent from your Gmail without your OK.

design.today: You answer messages many times a day, starting from scratch or from an old email. For a new inquiry you copy an old email and check your Sheet first.
design.newWay: Your common first replies live as saved Gmail templates, so a new inquiry starts from a ready email with a few gaps instead of an old email you have to clean up. You check your Sheet, fill in the gaps and send it yourself. For replies that need a little thought, Gmail's own writing help drafts a first version you can fix. Every reply still goes out in your voice and only after you read it.

steps.goal: Save instructions about you and your wedding planning business so every draft sounds like you.
Pick the handful of messages you answer most, such as a new inquiry, a call request and a pricing question, and gather your best past replies.
Turn those replies into Gmail templates with clear gaps for names, dates and budget.
Use Gmail's built in writing help for replies that each need a little thought.

material.what: Your most common replies, such as the first inquiry reply and the call request, with gaps to fill in.

material.label: Gap checklist
material.what: A short list of what to fill in each time, like the couple's names, wedding date, budget and call time.

design.checkPoint: You fill in every gap, check the date and budget against your Sheet, read the email and press Send yourself.

design.today: You write these by hand whenever a vendor goes quiet.
design.newWay: Once a week you get a list of vendors who have not answered you, so nobody slips by unnoticed. For the ones you choose, a follow up is drafted from the email thread in your Gmail in your usual tone. You read each draft and approve it, and nothing is sent without your OK. You stop writing chasers from scratch and stop relying on memory to know who has gone quiet.
